speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked	the Minister for Transport with regard to the collapse of the viaduct near the PIE exit to TPE (a) what is the cause of the collapse; (b) how does LTA assess and grade the contractors in the tender process, especially for companies with serious workplace safety lapses; and (c) what measures will be implemented to enhance workplace safety.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	 the Minister for Transport whether past safety records of construction firms is a consideration in awarding bids for Government construction projects.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) what caused the collapse of the viaduct under construction in Upper Changi Road East; (b) whether there have been previous sentinel events detected which could have raised concerns sooner; and (c) to what extent will prior serious workplace safety lapses affect a contractor's grading in the LTA tender process.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport in the past three years (a) how many tender submissions have been received by LTA from contractors with prior serious workplace safety lapses; (b) how many have been successful in their bids and how many have been the lowest bid, respectively; and (c) of the successful lowest bids from these contractors, what has been the median proportionate difference in the bid amount compared to the second lowest bid.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked	 the Minister for Transport (a) whether the contract for the collapsed viaduct near PIE was awarded to the lowest bidder who participated in the tender as the main contractor; (b) how are safety records of tenderers taken into consideration when evaluating tenders for the construction of transport infrastructure; and (c) in the last five years, how many contracts involving the construction of transport infrastructure have exceeded the planned construction period by three months or more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	the Minister for Transport with regard to the collapse of an uncompleted viaduct on 14 July 2017 (a) whether any extra checks are put in place when a construction company is blacklisted for a past incident while it is fulfilling a current contract for a public project; and (b) how does the Ministry seek to prevent future instances from happening.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked﻿	 the Minister for Transport (a) what is the weight given to workplace safety track record relative to bid price and other factors in the awarding of tenders to companies for the construction of the transport infrastructure; and (b) how was the workplace safety track record of the companies that took part in the tender for the construction of the PIE-TPE viaduct that collapsed evaluated relative to their bid prices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is working with MOM and BCA to investigate the cause of the collapse.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, we will have to wait till the investigations are completed to understand why they gave way.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Members have asked about LTA's procurement process for construction projects.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA adheres to the guidelines issued by BCA, which consider both the price and quality of bids.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: BCA's guidelines for the price-quality ratio range from 60:40 for more complex projects, to 80:20 for simpler ones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As part of the overall quality score, LTA assesses the safety practices of the bidders, based on their past safety records, such as their demerit points from MOM, the safety performance of their ongoing projects and the robustness of their safety management systems.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Tenderers who have had workplace safety lapses in the past would receive lower quality scores.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If a bidder does not meet minimum overall quality requirements, his price envelope will not even be opened, and his bid will be disqualified.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Two years ago, LTA further tightened the evaluation process, so that poor safety performance alone can lead to disqualification.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Over the past three years, LTA has called a total of 175 tenders for construction works, which received over 1,100 submissions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Out of these submissions, 69 were from contractors who had serious workplace safety lapses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Both these bidders had submitted the lowest price bid and received the highest overall price-quality score.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For these two cases, the winning price bids were 27% and 6% lower than the second lowest bids.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As for Mr Ang Wei Neng's query on project delays, out of 67 major rail and road projects that LTA has completed in the past five years, only seven exceeded the project timelines by more than three months.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In this particular case, the main contractor, Or Kim Peow Pte Ltd (OKP) had a fatal workplace incident at Yio Chu Kang Flyover in 2015.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOM's investigations were still ongoing at the time LTA was evaluating OKP's bid for the construction of this viaduct in question and, hence, LTA did not disqualify OKP outright.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Nevertheless, LTA gave OKP a low safety performance score in the evaluation of its bid.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the other hand, OKP offered the lowest tender price and also had a good track record in completing many similar infrastructural projects over the past 10 years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Overall, it obtained the highest score and was awarded the project.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Following the incident, LTA conducted a half-day safety timeout for all ongoing road and rail construction projects to review on-site safety practices and measures.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MOM inspected all active OKP worksites and other projects with ongoing viaduct works, and will step up inspection of other worksites performing formwork and concreting works.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will undertake all possible measures to prevent similar accidents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It pertains to how the contract was awarded to OKP for the tender.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: While I recognise that the outcome of the earlier incident was not finalised, the fact is that there was a fatality in the Yio Chu Kang Flyover project and there were three injuries as well.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my question is − notwithstanding the two-envelope system, notwithstanding that the outcome of the earlier incident was not finalised − I contend and I want the Ministry's view on this, on whether this has to be taken into account, regardless of whether the report is still outstanding.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The fact also is that the winning bid and the next winning bid were a massive 34% apart.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I know we are always smarter with hindsight, but I think these are serious lessons, and serious enough that, going forward, the lessons should be put into practice.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It should be documented and it should be instituted, so that future tenders on this two-envelope system adhere to the principle and intention of why we have a two-envelope system.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The tender submissions were evaluated objectively and fairly, based on the price-quality weightages and tender specifications made known to all the tenderers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While I understand that there are concerns with regard to the safety records of companies who are tendering for such projects, and although OKP has one fatality and some injuries at the Yio Chu Kang Flyover in September 2015, at the point in time when the tender was evaluated, like I mentioned in my reply, investigations were still ongoing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: OKP had a good track record over the past 10 years for completing many similar projects and, prior to the Yio Chu Kang Flyover accident, OKP had achieved an accident-free record of more than 25,000 man-hours.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Following the fatal accident at the Yio Chu Kang Flyover, OKP had also improved their safety standards with visible improvements.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since 2015, OKP did not have any work-site accidents, MOM fines or demerit points until the collapse of the current PIE-TPE viaduct.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We do take into consideration the safety records and safety performances of companies when they bid for projects.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: For design-and-build tenders, I know a good track record is important, but how do we evaluate the technical competency of the project site team and the contractors, such as the one involved in the erection of the working platform and temporary works?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: There were also reports of 11 cracks that were discovered after the incident.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share the investigations that are still ongoing?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The third question is whether there is a process in place to brief the site team for the temporary work, such as the loading, the PE design and the risk assessment for it.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, allow me to run through with Members our tender evaluation framework with regard to price, as well as the quality.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I have mentioned in my reply, all public agencies adhere to the price-quality method (PQM) published by BCA, which evaluates both the price as well as the quality attributes for all tenderers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For build-only projects, agencies generally adopt a price-quality weightage of 80:20.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In this case, which is a design-and-build project, agencies can consider price-quality ratios between 60:40 and 70:30, depending on the complexity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: BCA guidelines make it mandatory for safety performance to make up at least 15% of the quality score.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, LTA, in its internal guidelines, assigned 25%, so they are actually more stringent than BCA.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, 25% of the quality score must be attributed to safety performance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, LTA evaluates four sub-components for safety performance, namely, the safety records of the past two years, the robustness of the safety management systems, the safety and health performance in ongoing LTA projects and whether the company had won any safety awards.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Other components of the quality evaluation include project-specific proposals which actually form the bulk of the evaluation − project performance, dispute resolution approach and favourable adjudication result.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In this case, LTA had done the due diligence in ensuring that the award had been given to the tenderer who actually performed best in the PQM.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's question on the reasons and the cause of the accident, the investigation is ongoing; it is still premature to judge what is the exact cause.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I think it is unfair to make any judgement at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA, together with BCA and MOM, has already done whatever possible to put proppings around the structure to ensure that the existing structure remains safe for any ongoing investigation and works.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Senior Minister of State happen to have information on whether of these two successful bids from such contractors with such a safety lapse history, were there any subsequent serious safety lapses on these projects after the contractor won the bid in these two cases?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My second supplementary question is: in the event of a serious safety lapse, such as a fatality, to what extent would that shift the quality assessment of the contractor's subsequent bids?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The background to this, Mdm Speaker, is I am wondering whether there is a risk that some contractors may already be pricing in the impact of safety compliance and whether this may shape contractor behaviour.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the first, where two bidders were eventually successful out of the 69 bidders who had a serious safety lapse, I do not have the details of the kind of projects and works that they have been involved in.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I will be able to provide the information separately to him.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the impact of safety records on quality performance, yes, I have indicated in my previous reply that safety forms a significant proportion of the quality score.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While safety lapses may have happened, we also need to be cognisant of the fact that we need to go into the details of the accident − what caused the accident − before deciding on the score under the quality framework.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the end of the day, we need to look into all different factors and considerations and apply the PQM in determining who the eventual winner of the bid will be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I was just wondering whether there is a vicious cycle that is going on here in the sense that contractors, knowing that they will be scoring low for quality due to poor safety record, will be lowering their price bid in the next contract to an unrealistic level and, therefore, risking further safety lapses; and whether, therefore, a review of the PQM framework is on the cards after this accident.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA does not bar contractors which have safety lapses or are blacklisted by MOM from participating in the tenders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, their quality envelopes will still be opened and assessed objectively.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Any safety lapses will then be penalised under the safety component accordingly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, those with very low-quality scores may be disqualified and their price envelopes left unopened.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For such cases, the price envelopes will be returned unopened.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On the other hand, I also hope that LTA will not overdo it and have knee-jerk reaction.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Since the Stop Work Order is already issued, how much of a delay will this cause to the project?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, will the Ministry work with MOM to let the contractor resume work at other areas except the viaduct construction, because the project is a big project and now the Stop Work Order is for the whole project?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is working with MOM as well as BCA to investigate the cause of the collapse.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, the delay of the project after the issuance of the Stop Work Order will depend on the investigation process and the cause of the accident.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Once that has been determined, all necessary precautions, as well as, if there is a need in re-qualifying the design and so on, will be taken into consideration before work can resume.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, please keep your supplementary question short.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We know that in the construction industry, it is typical for these main contractors to have multiple subsidiary companies.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, how are these taken into account, especially if the subsidiary companies had previous safety lapses, in the overall assessment if the award is being tendered by another company within this whole holdings?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second question is, because of this complexity or the scale of the project, it is typical to have multiple sub-contractors.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How does the main contractor ensure that the sub-contractors actively take measures against all these safety lapses?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For all projects, ultimately, the main contractor will be held responsible for any safety lapses that may occur as a result of the work that has been sublet to other smaller subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, what measures will be taken to ensure that the project will continue as smoothly and as safely as possible?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second supplementary question is: is the Senior Minister of State able to give an estimated timeline of when the investigation will be completed and will the report be made public?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Once the investigation has been completed, we will make public the report as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to how soon we can resume work, we will resume as soon as possible, without compromising safety.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: A supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The most recent one, unfortunately, the findings were not complete and, therefore, it was not quite taken into account.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: My question to him is, while it is important to look into the 10-year track record, more weightage should be given to the recency effect, the most recent incident.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I asked this earlier, he did not quite nail it down, I want to ask again.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Would such things be instituted in future tender awards?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This PQM really needs to be reviewed, taking into account that notwithstanding that most recent incidents have not been finalised, it must be taken as a factor, to be seriously deliberated and considered.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I hope this will be factored in, going forward.
